title: Subsets with Duplicates
statement:
Produce every distinct subset of a collection of integers that may contain repeated values.

Contract
- `values` may be empty and may contain equal numbers.
- Return every distinct subset once. Two subsets are the same when they hold the same numbers the same number of times, regardless of which positions the numbers came from.
- The empty subset is always included. The order of the subsets and of the numbers inside a subset do not matter.
- Each returned subset must be its own list, and `values` must not be changed.

Examples
- `subsets(new int[]{1, 2, 2})` returns `[[], [1], [2], [1, 2], [2, 2], [1, 2, 2]]` in any order.
- `subsets(new int[]{4, 4, 4})` returns `[[], [4], [4, 4], [4, 4, 4]]`.
- `subsets(new int[]{0})` returns `[[], [0]]` in any order.
hints: If equal numbers sit next to each other, choosing the first or the second copy of a number gives the same subset. Sorting a copy of the values makes equal numbers adjacent.

Build subsets by choosing which value to add next from the remaining positions. When you loop over the candidates for the next slot, skip a value that equals the one tried just before it in the same loop.

The skip applies only to alternatives for the same slot; a repeated value may still follow its own earlier copy deeper in the path. The probe uses n copies of one value, which gives n + 1 subsets of total length about n^2 / 2. Intended complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space for that family; in general the output can hold 2^n subsets.
inputSyntax: Input: the values as a list, for example: [1, 2, 2]
